# Teleoperation

## What can be teleoperated?

::: {.teleoperation-scope-intro}
Teleoperation converts joystick or keyboard inputs into commands adapted to
each controllable part of the robot.
:::

::: {.teleoperation-scope-grid}
::: {.teleoperation-scope-item}
**Mobile base**

- Linear and angular velocity
- Front and rear steering angles
- Skid, omni, one-axle and two-axle kinematics
:::

::: {.teleoperation-scope-item}
**Integrated actuators**

- Front or rear three-point hitches
- Lift and telescopic arms
:::
:::

::: {.teleoperation-scope-flow}
![](img/07_teleoperation/teleoperation_scope_flow.svg){.teleoperation-scope-flow-diagram}

One input device can drive several teleoperation nodes. Each robot subsystem
keeps its own command mux and controller, so manual commands can coexist with
other command sources.
:::

##  Base teleoperation configuration

::: {.columns .config-slide .teleoperation-config-slide}
::: {.column width="50%"}

#### Configuration files

::: {.config-path}

```text
config/
  robot/
    teleop.yaml
    base.yaml
    devices/
      remote_controller.joystick.yaml
```

:::

```yaml
cmd_output:
  # Select the command matching the mobile base:
  message_type: romea_mobile_base_msgs/SkidSteeringCommand
  # message_type: romea_mobile_base_msgs/OneAxleSteeringCommand
  # message_type: romea_mobile_base_msgs/TwoAxleSteeringCommand
  message_priority: 100

cmd_range:
  maximal_linear_speed:
    slow_mode: 1.0
    turbo_mode: 2.0

  # SkidSteeringCommand
  maximal_angular_speed:
    slow_mode: 1.0
    turbo_mode: 2.0

  # OneAxleSteeringCommand
  # maximal_steering_angle: 0.6

  # TwoAxleSteeringCommand
  # maximal_front_steering_angle: 0.6
  # maximal_rear_steering_angle: 0.6
```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

#### Key fields

::: {.config-table}

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `message_type` | Matches the mobile-base kinematics |
| `message_priority` | Registers teleoperation in `base/cmd_mux` |
| `slow_mode` | Limits commands for precise manoeuvres |
| `turbo_mode` | Enables the extended speed range |
| steering/angular limits | Bound the corresponding command |

:::

#### Command families

::: {.config-table}

| Kinematics | Command message |
| --- | --- |
| Skid/differential | `SkidSteeringCommand` |
| One steering axle / 2WS | `OneAxleSteeringCommand` |
| Two steering axles / 4WS4WD | `TwoAxleSteeringCommand` |
| Omnidirectional | `OmniSteeringCommand` |

:::

Teleoperation normally uses a higher mux priority than autonomous
path-following commands, so the operator can immediately take control.

:::
:::

## Keyboard mapping

::: {.keyboard-mapping-intro}
The `pynput_teleop` node converts keyboard events into the same
`sensor_msgs/msg/Joy` interface as a physical controller.
:::

::: {.keyboard-mapping-figure}
![](img/07_teleoperation/teleop_keyboard_qwerty.svg)
:::

::: {.keyboard-mapping-note}
- The arrow keys always mean **Forward**, **Reverse**, **Left** and **Right**,
  while the selected teleoperation node converts these inputs into commands
  matching the mobile-base kinematics.
- The `two_axle_steering` teleoperation node applies double-Ackermann steering:
  `rear_steering_angle = -front_steering_angle`.
- Keyboard teleoperation currently controls one configured implement at a time.
:::
